Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position serves as a senior Human Resources Specialist that applies the full range of HR methods and principles to advise management on staffing requirements, resources, and personnel issues for the Europe District of the US Army Corps of Engineers.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Advise management on recruitment strategies, special programs, and incentives. Provide guidance on merit system principles, prohibited personnel practices, selection criteria, and other approaches that may help with staffing and employee retention.

Explain procedures to inquiring employees, candidates, and supervisors. Complete necessary documents on personnel actions. Maintain visibility over recruitment actions from cradle to grave and aid in all stages of the recruitment process.
Construct job analyses to determine the specialized knowledge, skills, abilities, and other competencies necessary for the recruitment and placement of well-qualified individuals.

Prepare vacancy announcements for Federal civilian positions using USA Staffing or similar automated vacancy announcement system, ensuring information contained in the vacancy announcement meets agency requirements.
Code personnel actions based on the Guide to Processing Personnel Actions utilizing an automated HR system such as the Defense Civilian Personnel Data System (DCPDS).
Advise on overseas policies, to include tour rotations, travel regulations, and pay entitlements. Ensure overseas regulations are understood and enforced.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Wiesbaden is without a doubt one of the most attractive cities in Germany. The capital city of Hessen is sometimes referred to as "Nice of the North" and rightfully so considering the many mansions, the historic Kurhaus, the casino and the State Theater. Wiesbaden has 27 hot, saline springs and its mild climate and park-like setting continue to make it a popular resort and conference center. Wiesbaden is a city with an abundance of leisure activities, providing a cosmopolitan atmosphere blended with an attractive cultural ambiance, extraordinary architecture and marked by endearing charm. Wiesbaden, located in one of the premier wine growing areas in Germany, is on the Rhine River only 20 minutes from the Frankfurt International Airport. Efficient mass transportation systems are readily available. Visit the Wiesbaden Army Community website at: www.wiesbaden.army.mil for local garrison support and http://www.wiesbaden.de for city plans and attractions.
MajorDuties: Serve as Chief of Human Resources, advising and providing guidance and assistance to commanders, managers, senior staff, supervisors, and employees on all areas of Civilian personnel management regulations, policies, and laws.

Responsible for staff direction and administration of a comprehensive HR management program involving both civilian and military personnel management throughout Command including HQ, Directorates and Garrisons world-wide.

Applying advanced Human Resources (HR) principles, theories, concepts, and practices involving the full spectrum of HR functions (e.g., Civilian Personnel Management; Army Continuing Education System (ACES); Workforce Development Programs).
Oversees supervisory and non-supervisory personnel in the Human Resources Division in eight distinctly different program areas and subordinate organizations.
Functions as the primary Region Transformation Manager for a multitude of highly complex transformation activities and programs.

Provides input to Region guidelines and manages the Region's Military Personnel Management Program, Supports the Director, IMCOM-Europe in providing advice and guidance for the Region's Retention Program.
Ensures adherence to applicable international agreements and treaties as well as, host country labor laws in the administration and management of the local national work forces.
